characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Specimen ϕ6 mm × 9 mm; tantalum foil (0.1 mm) at specimen/indenter interfaces.
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure flow stress under constant and varying deformation conditions.

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Sections ground with SiC papers, polished with 1 µm and 0.25 µm diamond pastes, etched with saturated picric acid solution.
characterization_methods.purpose: Observe prior austenite grain (PAG) microstructure at the center of the side section.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: SU5000 scanning electron microscope equipped with an EBSD detector; step size 0.65–1.3 µm
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: EBSD samples electrolytically polished with 10 % perchlorate alcohol solution at 30 V and 0.25 A for 30 s.
characterization_methods.purpose: Characterize as-quenched martensitic microstructure and reconstruct prior austenite grains.

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Reconstructed austenite EBSD maps using the Greninger-Troiano (GT) orientation relationship.
characterization_methods.purpose: Reconstruct prior austenite grains from as-quenched martensite EBSD maps.
characterization_methods.technique: Prior austenite grain reconstruction from EBSD

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Equivalent diameter of each prior austenite grain calculated based on corresponding area in metallography.
characterization_methods.purpose: Calculate equivalent diameter of each prior austenite grain (PAG).
characterization_methods.technique: Image analysis for equivalent grain diameter

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Recrystallized grains distinguished from deformed grains using GOS values with threshold 3°; PAG equivalent diameter calculated considering boundaries with misorientation >10°.
characterization_methods.purpose: Distinguish recrystallized grains from deformed grains and measure DRX fraction.

computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: Initial dislocation density 1×10^11 m^-2; load condition: 950 °C, stage I 0.01 s^-1 to ε=0.4, stage II 0.1 s^-1 to ε_total=0.9.
computational_details.simulation_method: 3D cellular automaton (CA) with inhomogeneous dislocation density for DRX simulation
computational_details.software_used: custom 3D CA model; RVE 550 µm × 550 µm × 550 µm, cell size L0 = 2.5 µm
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Under varying deformation conditions (Table 5): flow stress RMSE 3.3118 MPa, R² 0.9589, AARE 4.57 %; AGS RMSE 4.0169 µm, R² 0.9777, AARE 4.11 %; DRX fraction RMSE 0.0229, R² 0.9784, AARE 2.47 %.

analytical_models.equation_role: Thermal, softening/DRX, flow-stress and nucleation/growth kinetics constants
analytical_models.model_note: Parameters obtained by genetic algorithm optimization (Appendix A2).

analytical_models.equation_role: CA-model constants (GBS, nucleation, grain growth, dislocation interaction)
analytical_models.model_note: Parameters from literature or solved by GA optimization (Appendix B1).

computational_details.simulation_method: Material parameters for constitutive model and 3D CA model
Finite element simulation of hot compression
computational_details.software_used: DEFORM 3D (constitutive model embedded via Fortran language)
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Simulation accuracy verified by comparison with experimental results under constant and varying deformation conditions.

interfaces.interface_notes: Prior austenite grain boundaries reconstructed using boundaries with misorientation >10°; GOS threshold 3° used to distinguish recrystallized grains.
interfaces.phase_evolution: First-stage DRX grains nucleate at matrix grain boundaries; after the strain-rate increase, second-stage DRX grains nucleate at boundaries of the matrix and first-stage DRX grains.
interfaces.slip_behavior: Dislocation slip and grain-boundary sliding (GBS) are considered in the inhomogeneous-dislocation-density CA model.

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Isothermal holding at 950 °C for 60 s before compression.
First stage deformed to fixed strain ε=0.4 at 950 °C and strain rate ε̇I=0.01 s^-1.
Strain rate transiently increased from 0.01 s^-1 to 0.1 s^-1 at ε=0.4, then compressed to total strain ε_total=0.9.

measurement_conditions.environment: Gleeble 1500 thermomechanical simulator; tantalum foil (0.1 mm) between specimen ends and indenter to prevent interfacial melting and minimize friction.
measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Compressed to total strain 0.9; water quenched immediately after deformation.
measurement_conditions.strain_rate: 0.01 s^-1 (stage I) → 0.1 s^-1 (stage II), transient increase at ε=0.4

tensile_properties.stress_strain_curves: Hot-compression true stress–strain curve at 950 °C for transient strain-rate increase 0.01→0.1 s^-1 at εI=0.4. After the step, stress rises abruptly at ε≈0.4, then develops a peak and subsequent softening. No numeric stress values were extracted from the figures (Fig. 8a,b and Fig. 13a).

grain_structure.grain_size_distribution: 2D AGS 141.66 µm, SD 54.54 µm, Min 10.22 µm, Max 265.20 µm (experimental); 3D AGS 143.78 µm, SD 58.25 µm, Min 6.45 µm, Max 283.29 µm (CA 3D); face d_ave 166.00 µm (top), 131.59 µm (right), 127.63 µm (left).

phases_present.morphology: mixed-grain structure of coarse and fine equiaxed grains

microstructure_list.region: Representative orthogonal sections (side/top) of the initial microstructure

structures.overall_structure: Mixed-grain prior austenite (PAG) initial microstructure before deformation.

microstructure_list.region: Side section / reconstructed PAG microstructure at 0.9 strain

structures.overall_structure: Nearly complete recrystallized austenite at 0.9 strain, composed of first-stage (DRXGs_I) and second-stage (DRXGs_II) DRX grains.

unmapped_findings: For this sample (950 °C, 0.01→0.1 s^-1 transient at ε=0.4), the experimental DRX fraction increased from 75.7 % at 0.4 strain to 84.6 % at 0.5 strain after the strain-rate increase, and reached 95.8 % (experiment) / 97.9 % (3D CA) at 0.9 strain (sources: b0220, figure_018, b0213).

DRX fraction evolution for 'Increasing ε̇ at 0.4 strain' (figure_018, b0213): Experiment 0.757 at 0.4 strain, 0.846 at 0.5 strain, 0.958 at 0.9 strain; 3D CA 0.769 at 0.4 strain, 0.859 at 0.5 strain, 0.979 at 0.9 strain.

After transiently increasing strain rate at 0.4 strain, only a few second-stage DRX grains (marked red in simulation) began nucleation within a 0.1 strain interval, limiting microstructure refinement; consequently the simulated AGS at 0.5 strain was larger than that at a constant rate of 0.1 s^-1 (source: b0220).
